comments.author: MacDue
comments.body: It looks like a disjoint ORR has been emitted rather than an ADD, which is missing handling in a few places.

comments.author: MacDue
efriedma-quic
comments.body: I'd prefer we not do that... flags like "disjoint" are supposed to be droppable.  We just shouldn't generate an ORR with a frame index operand.

comments.author: MacDue
comments.body:
Hmmm. I tried that:

```diff
diff --git a/llvm/lib/CodeGen/SelectionDAG/DAGCombiner.cpp b/llvm/lib/CodeGen/SelectionDAG/DAGCombiner.cpp
index aba3c0f80a02..5fdc9add33d8 100644
--- a/llvm/lib/CodeGen/SelectionDAG/DAGCombiner.cpp
+++ b/llvm/lib/CodeGen/SelectionDAG/DAGCombiner.cpp
@@ -3015,7 +3015,7 @@ SDValue DAGCombiner::visitADD(SDNode *N) {
 
   // fold (a+b) -> (a|b) iff a and b share no bits.
   if ((!LegalOperations || TLI.isOperationLegal(ISD::OR, VT)) &&
-      DAG.haveNoCommonBitsSet(N0, N1))
+      !isa<FrameIndexSDNode>(N0) && DAG.haveNoCommonBitsSet(N0, N1))
     return DAG.getNode(ISD::OR, DL, VT, N0, N1, SDNodeFlags::Disjoint);
 
   // Fold (add (vscale * C0), (vscale * C1)) to (vscale * (C0 + C1)).
```

comments.author: efriedma-quic
comments.body: This is a statepoint-specific issue.  Normally, we don't generate ORR with a frameindex operand.  But the Statepoint code uses TargetFrameIndex, which tricks the lowering code into doing weird things with it.  We shouldn't be using TargetFrameIndex as an operand to a target-independent node like a load or an add.
